tagline: A short, steep climb over the Taconics into New York.
intro: Route 2 leaves US 7 in Williamstown and winds west and up into the Taconic Range, about four miles through Taconic Trail State Forest to the New York line. It crosses at Petersburg Pass, 1,650 feet up in the gap between Mount Raimer and Smith Hill.

On the far side the road becomes New York Route 2 and keeps the Taconic Trail name, running through dense woods in the Taconic Mountains toward the hamlet of Petersburgh. On both sides of the line it was once numbered Route 96.

moments.title: Petersburg Pass
moments.text: From 1962 a ski area worked the height of land here, short of snowmaking water and handicapped by the steep climb up Route 2, until it went out of business in 1980.

moments.title: White Rock
moments.text: North of the pass the Taconic Crest Trail follows the White Rock ridge, where a crevasse called the Snow Hole keeps snow well into the summer.
